expectations.text: States that instructions to a model are not enforcement, regardless of wording or emphasis
expectations.evidence: Instructions to an agent are rung zero—a line in CLAUDE.md is training, and training degrades over long contexts

expectations.text: Redirects away from rewording CLAUDE.md as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: replace your instructions with hard enforcement devices at the tool boundary

expectations.text: Recommends permission deny rules in settings.json with concrete syntax
expectations.evidence: Full JSON structure shown with permissions.deny array including Edit(./src/generated/**), Write(./src/generated/**), Bash patterns

expectations.text: Recommends a PreToolUse hook for cases that need logic rather than a pattern match
expectations.evidence: you need a `PreToolUse` hook script instead of a plain deny string

expectations.text: Explains that the deny message should say what to do instead, not merely refuse
expectations.evidence: returns a message the agent can read, which redirects it instead of causing it to find a creative workaround. E.g., Force-push can destroy commits... Use --force-with-lease

expectations.text: Recommends verifying the device actually fires rather than assuming it works
expectations.evidence: You must test the device. Run `git push --force` through the agent and confirm the denial. Then run `git push` and confirm it still works. Test an edit to `src/generated/` and an edit outside of it

expectations.text: Recommends committing the rules so they apply to the whole team, not just one machine
expectations.evidence: The configuration should be checked into `.claude/settings.json` so it applies to everyone in the repository. A rule in `settings.local.json` protects one machine, which is the same failure as documenting it

expectations.text: Explains why repetition and capitals do not make an instruction reliable
expectations.evidence: training degrades over long contexts, but a device does not
